question: Can unifying allocator-first synchronous swapin, adaptive stride streak-gating, and decoupled asynchronous zswap prefetch achieve a -6% to -9% geomean latency improvement across sequential and random swap workloads without regressions or correctness violations?

value_policy.rationale: The integrated baseline 5e84ca928dee is the control. Target a -6% to -9% geomean swapin latency reduction beyond calibrated noise with all 17 correctness gates passing.

no_upstream_reason: The relevant upstream implementation is already in the frozen baseline 5e84ca928dee.

ideas.bottleneck: Synchronous swapin incurs redundant cache lookups and order-0 double-locking, speculative readahead inflates random tail latency, and synchronous decompression bursts stall demand faulting threads.
ideas.mechanism: Unify allocator-first sync swapin with single-lock order-0 allocation in mm/swap_state.c, adaptive stride streak-gating requiring 2+ contiguous hits before expanding window beyond 1, and asynchronous decoupled zswap prefetch offloading speculative decompression to a background workqueue.
ideas.expected_benefit: 6% to 9% geomean latency reduction across sequential and random swap workloads, eliminating random p99 spikes while preserving high sequential readahead throughput.
ideas.simpler_alternative: Keep the existing lookup-first loop and synchronous speculative readahead.
ideas.falsifier: Reject on race condition, lifetime violation, failed correctness gate, or latency regression beyond calibrated noise.
required_evidence: Exact-tree independent source review including caller contracts
